items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: And of course, the guy who was responsible for me being there, Pee Wee Moore, was there.

ctx.x: But one of the most, I would say, significant people in the band, for more than one reason, was a young man who was 18 years old at that particular time. His name was Oliver Nelson. I was amazed at this guy, because he had written the whole book for the band, and it was rather an extensive book. Besides all of Louis' things, he'd written a lot of other original things. And he played saxophone very well.
Money Johnson, another trumpet player, was in the band. And of course, the guy who was responsible for me being there, Pee Wee Moore, was there.

Altogether, it was a very nice and different kind of experience, because being in a band like that was quite different than anything that I had been in. First of all, the kind of stuff that Louis Jordan was doing, after coming out of a band like the Eckstine band, with Charlie Parker and people like that. You know, we were sitting up playing this shuffle rhythm, and these almost... What we played were usually...80 percent vocals that Louis sang during the night.
